title: Error-Mitigated Hamiltonian Simulation: Complexity Analysis and Optimization for Near-Term and Early-Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
summary: Simulating real-time dynamics under a Hamiltonian is a central goal of quantum information science. While numerous Hamiltonian-simulation quantum algorithms have been proposed, the effects of physical noise have rarely been incorporated into their performance analysis, despite the non-negligible noise levels of quantum devices. We present an end-to-end complexity analysis of noisy Hamiltonian simulation combined with quantum error mitigation (QEM) to answer how many circuit runs are required to reach a given target accuracy.
